result.stopReason: Relaxing checkP alone is unsound, and closing the hole is a second design decision, which is the stop CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:85 names for this rung. checkP is not an accident of the checker. It is the Fortress designers' own rule, "multiple instantiation exclusion": the OOPSLA 2011 paper adopts it by name (Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152), and Naden's 2012-08-31 writeup says "Fortress implements blanket multiple instantiation exclusion" (Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497). The compiled checker's Return Type Rule check solves for a single instantiation of the generic, which is sound only while that rule holds (OverloadingOracle.scala:81-105). A six-line BadList program shows the hole: probes/ProbeMIEPick.fss has object Both extends {Tag[String], Tag[ZZ32]}, a generic pick[X] beside a pick specialised for Tag[ZZ32], and y: Tag[String] = pick(Both). With the relaxation it type-checks under all three placements (hierarchy only, hierarchy plus overloading, broad) and dies with IncompatibleClassChangeError: IntTag does not implement Tag[String] (probe-matrix.txt:67, :89, :111). The base checker refuses the program. Making the compiled path sound again needs one of two choices, and both are Pavol's. Either keep the rule on the compiled path, and then the interpreter library's nested tower cannot be checked as it stands. Or drop the rule together with enforcing Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-105 (declarations whose static parameters differ are an error), which is decision (b) of perf-probes/nat/triage.md:52-59, :113, already reserved to him.

result.summary:
Rung P stopped and lands no checker change. The clause it was to relax, checkP, is the Fortress designers' "multiple instantiation exclusion" (OOPSLA 2011, Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152; Naden 2012, justificationOfRTR.tex:476-478, :496-497). The compiled checker enforces it in the two hierarchy questions and relies on it in the Return Type Rule check (OverloadingOracle.scala:81-105). The trace, the triage and the batch record never cite it. The batch record's "designers' survey" is a revival-era note (run-c4/.../D/SURVEY.md:46).
All measurements used one build with an instance-held switch (probes/measurement-switch.patch); the source tree is back at the base.
Under every placement (hierarchy only, hierarchy plus overloading, broad) a six-line BadList program type-checks and dies with IncompatibleClassChangeError: a variable typed Tag[String] holds an object that is only a Tag[ZZ32]. The base checker refuses the program.
The interpreter took the other side of the trade-off. It has no instantiation clause, and it refuses generic overloads that have no excluding pair. The specification sides with the interpreter on both halves (types-vals-vars.tex:184-189; overloading.tex:100-105). Rung P as briefed is the one unsound combination: the interpreter's half on inheritance with the compiler's half on overloading.

The rung landed. TypeAnalyzer.parents and excludesClause are now memoized on TraitTable behind one switch, fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache (default on). In TypeAnalyzer.scala only the two def lines (:722, :747) change: each passes its unchanged body to traits.memoParents or traits.memoExcludesClause. No line is added there, so rung P's line numbers are unchanged. TraitTable gains 20 lines: ConcurrentHashMap maps filled by get then putIfAbsent, because excludesClause recurses into its own map.
Soundness: both functions read only the table and the type (typeCons, and the pure substitute). TraitTable has no mutator. The index clauses change only while an index is being built. Every "new" trait table is a new object with empty memos (eight construction sites). The checker is single-threaded.
The count-stage table is identical line for line: 93 before and after. Differentials, memo on against off: the prelude's 556 class files and 14 analyzed-cache files are byte-identical. All 435 compiler_tests units give identical compile output, and the 2,049 class files and 230 analyzed-cache files they leave are identical. Six analyzer JUnit classes pass both ways.
Timing (probes/timing.txt): the stage takes 22.3-22.6 s with the memo off and 9.5-12.4 s with it on. The prelude build took 196 s off and 129 s on (one run each).
The batch record's "21 s to 13 s" compared the nat shadow with the stock tree. Setup: the launch had not created this worktree or branch, so the rung created both from d610695c0 with the recipe in remote-container.md. Suites not run, by the batch rule.
decisions: The switch is read on TraitTable beside the memo, not in TypeAnalyzer.scala's block of seven at :62-69. Rejected alternative: a val in that block (the exact precedent position). Reasons: the brief says nothing else in TypeAnalyzer.scala should change, and two lines added there would shift every line of the file rung P edits.

One switch for both memos (fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache). Rejected alternative: one switch per memo, as the analyzer's block does. The single switch follows the prototype (shadow.patch:667-668) and TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:53, which guards its two sibling memos with one switch.

The maps are java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap, filled by get then putIfAbsent. Rejected alternative: scala.collection.mutable.HashMap, which all ten existing checker memos use. The table is the object every analyzer of a check shares, the concurrent map costs nothing, and computeIfAbsent was rejected because excludesClause recurses into the same map.

Each existing body is wrapped in a by-name argument at its def line. Rejected alternative: splitting each function into a wrapper plus an Inner function, as the shadow and pExc/pSub do. Wrapping keeps both bodies byte-identical and each TypeAnalyzer edit to one line.

One comment line in the source (TraitTable.scala:81) states the invariant the memo relies on. Rejected alternative: no comment. The line tells the next editor of parents or excludesClause what must stay true; it is not provenance.
